title: EPIDERMOLYSIS BULLOSA SIMPLEX 3, LOCALIZED OR GENERALIZED INTERMEDIATE, WITH BP230 DEFICIENCY

relationships.phenotype: EPIDERMOLYSIS BULLOSA SIMPLEX 3, LOCALIZED OR GENERALIZED INTERMEDIATE, WITH BP230 DEFICIENCY

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that epidermolysis bullosa simplex-3, localized or generalized intermediate, with BP230 deficiency (EBS3) is caused by homozygous mutation in the DST gene (113810) on chromosome 6p12.1, which encodes the epithelial isoform of bullous pemphigoid antigen-1 (BPAG1-e, also known as BP230).

checks.claim: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex-3, localized or generalized intermediate, with BP230 deficiency (EBS3) is caused by homozygous mutation in the DST gene.
checks.evidence_quote: A homozygous nonsense mutation within the dystonin gene coding for the coiled-coil domain of the epithelial isoform of BPAG1 underlies a new subtype of autosomal recessive epidermolysis bullosa simplex.
checks.explanation: Paper supports homozygous DST mutation causing a new AR EBS subtype (single patient); the 'localized or generalized intermediate' designation is not in the abstract, which describes generalized blistering.

checks.claim: The DST gene is located on chromosome 6p12.1.
checks.evidence_quote: We now report an inherited skin fragility disorder with a homozygous nonsense mutation in the dystonin gene (DST)
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature restating the gene; not stated in abstract itself.

checks.claim: The DST gene encodes the epithelial isoform of bullous pemphigoid antigen-1 (BPAG1-e), also known as BP230.
checks.evidence_quote: the dystonin gene (DST) that encodes the coiled-coil domain of the epithelial isoform of bullous pemphigoid antigen 1, BPAG1-e (also known as BP230)

paragraphs.text: EBS3 is an autosomal recessive form of epidermolysis bullosa simplex caused by loss of the epithelial isoform of dystonin, BPAG1-e (BP230), which results in loss of the hemidesmosomal inner plaques (Groves et al., 2010). Groves et al. (2010) described generalized trauma-induced blisters and erosions, particularly around the ankles. Epidermolysis bullosa simplex is characterized by skin fragility due to intraepidermal separation (Ganani et al., 2021).

checks.evidence_quote: identifying BPAG1-e pathology in a new form of autosomal recessive EB simplex

checks.explanation: Loss of BPAG1-e follows from complete absence of immunostaining due to nonsense mutation.

paragraphs.text: Groves et al. (2010) reported a patient with generalized trauma-induced blisters and erosions, particularly around the ankles. Hemidesmosomal inner plaques were lost, and skin immunostaining for BPAG1-e was completely absent. The patient also had episodic numbness in his limbs, which started at the age of 37 years. Groves et al. (2010) suggested that these neurologic symptoms may also be due to the DST mutation.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with autosomal recessive EBS, Groves et al. (2010) identified a homozygous nonsense mutation in the DST gene, resulting in a gln1124-to-ter (Q1124X) substitution in the coiled-coil domain of BPAG1-e. Skin immunostaining for BPAG1-e was completely absent in the patient.
